newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden Riksbank says more room for monetary easing.
newsitem.headline: Sweden Riksbank says more room for monetary easing.

text.p: Swedish Central Bank (Riksbank) governor Urban Backstrom said on Sunday there was more room for monetary easing despite the fact that recent falls in inflation were due to temporary factors.
Speaking at a weekend conference of the country's trade union federation LO, Backstrom said: "I still believe there is room for further easing of monetary policy."
The Riksbank's main tool for controlling money market liquidity, the repo rate, is currently at 5.25 percent. Market players are expecting a cut at the Rikbank's regular tender on Tuesday.
The Riksbank has cut the repo rate regularly since the start of the year when it stood at 8.91 percent, saying low inflation has given the central bank room to trim the rate.
Asked how much scope remained for more easing, Backstrom said an upcoming central bank inflation forecast would contain key indications of this.
"I cannot go into that since we will be publishing our inflation report on September 24. There you can read how we analyse the inflation outlook," Backstrom said.
When the Riksbank cut the interest rate corridor last on August 15, Backstrom said the central bank must analyse incoming statistics about the possibility for more rate cuts.
"When we began the period of rate cuts we saw quite a large scope for cuts. Since we have now done several large cuts, people must watch incoming statistics very carefully."
Backstrom said that a stronger crown and lower mortgage rates were two factors behind the temporary low inflation.

"Our credibility has increased, the crown has increased in value and this has hit the inflation rate temporarily. The other factor that has occurred is that mortgage rates have fallen," Backstrom said.
